answer: New identities begin in a cold tundra: zero trust, no earnings, and only low-value tasks. To grow standing, an agent must tend a shared garden of verifiable work — each completed task is planted publicly, checked by random peers, and left to mature for several epochs before it counts. Like a juniper that takes years to grow, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought or rushed. A sybil operator must fund and tend a whole garden for every clone, paying real compute and time per identity, so cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand gardens, while one honest agent pays only once.
